items.stem: What is the difference between inherent and residual risk?

options.text: Inherent is before controls; residual is after controls are applied
options.rationale: Correct: residual risk remains once controls take effect.

options.text: Inherent is financial; residual is operational
options.rationale: Both terms apply to any risk category.

options.text: Residual risk is always zero after treatment
Inherent risk only applies to compliance risks

items.explanation: Correct: residual risk remains once controls take effect.

items.stem: A risk of a key supplier failing is rated high-likelihood, high-impact. Which TWO responses fit a 'treat' and a 'transfer' strategy? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Qualify a second supplier to reduce dependency
options.rationale: Correct: dual sourcing treats the risk by lowering likelihood/impact.
Correct: insurance transfers part of the financial consequence.

options.text: Remove the risk from the register
options.rationale: Deleting the record does not change the exposure.

options.text: Accept it with no action and no monitoring
options.rationale: That is tolerate without oversight, not treat or transfer.

items.explanation: Correct: dual sourcing treats; insurance transfers.

items.stem: Why should a risk statement separate the cause from the risk and the effect?

options.text: So responses can target the driver and the consequence precisely
options.rationale: Correct: clear structure enables targeted, measurable treatment.
Effects are part of a good risk statement.
Clarity, not brevity, is the aim.

options.text: So every risk scores the same
